about: Growth and quality stock-picking, from a 'Tiger cub' hedge fund.
summary: 34 holdings; the top ten are 54% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 152% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 0.7 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are more expensive, more profitable, faster-growing and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 6 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1956; Dartmouth and Harvard. A consumer analyst at Goldman Sachs, then at Tiger Management, before founding Lone Pine Capital in 1997.
profile.note: Mandel stopped managing Lone Pine's investments in 2019; the holdings are chosen by the firm's other partners.

name: Stephen Mandel
